what_the_eye_sees: A plain, smooth gold comfort band, wide like a wedding band. One flat side edge carries a ring of 12 blue marquise stones pointing outward, with 12 small red round stones on the outer rim between them. With no caption it looks like a jewelled watch bezel, a compass rose or a gem-set flange washer. It does not look like a rose window, and nothing says Gothic cathedral. The only centre is the finger hole, so there is no hub and no window glass. There are no tracery bars, no foils or cusps and no pointed arches. The stones sit loose on a flat plain ledge with no frame of stone-work around them. From the side (side.png) the ring is a featureless polished band, and the stones barely show at the bottom edge.
changes: Give the window its own centre. Move the composition off the band's flank onto a raised round head on top of the shank, at least 15 mm across, slightly domed, with the head's axis pointing away from the finger. Put a central boss there: a round stone of 3 to 4 mm in a cusped bezel, set where the empty finger hole now sits in the face view. A rose window needs a hub. A ring of stones around a void reads as a washer or a bezel.

Add stone tracery. Run 12 radial mullion bars, about 0.6 to 0.8 mm wide and 0.8 mm proud, from the central boss to the rim between the petal openings. Put a cusped foil ring (6 to 8 foils, about 0.5 mm relief) around the boss. Give the outer edge a rim of small arches or foils, 24 cusps in place of the plain flat ring. Each blue marquise should sit in an open (à jour) lancet with a pointed-arch outer end, not on a flat plate. The red stones go into the small round openings between the arch heads (the eyes between arches). At 300 px the dark lines of the tracery must show as a spoked, foiled wheel.

Carry the cathedral onto the shank. Replace the plain smooth band with 2 to 3 tiers of shallow pointed-arch arcading or buttress ribs on each shoulder (about 0.6 mm relief, covering about 40 degrees on each side of the head). The side view should then read as stone-work holding up a window, not a plain wedding band.
